subject: APAC checkout impact — immediate geo-redirect and exec escalation
messages:
From: Liya Chen <liya@skylineretail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: skylineretail-ops@skylineretail.com
Date: 2028-05-26T03:12:00Z
Subject: Production: APAC checkout latency spike & 502s

Kimberly —

We're seeing a sudden ~10–20s tail latency on checkout API calls and a rising 502 rate from apac-1 (APAC zone 3) starting ~02:50 UTC. This is impacting ~12% of customers in APAC and causing SKU inventory errors at payment step. Attached a quick latency heatmap and our own error logs.

We urgently need a plan to avoid revenue loss. Can you confirm whether Redwood can divert traffic to our eu-2 endpoint as a temporary measure? Also, do you expect session/cookie issues if we fail over?

Contact: Liya Chen, Head of Infrastructure — Skyline Retail
Attachments: apac-latency-20280526.png, skyline-checkout-logs-526.txt
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Liya Chen <liya@skylineretail.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-26T03:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: APAC checkout latency spike & 502s

Thanks Liya — I'm on it. Sorry for the impact.

Quick summary of immediate actions I'm initiating:
- Looping in Aditya (infra) and Vivek (ops/exec) to triage and lead a short bridge.
- Preparing a targeted geo-redirect (apac->eu-2) for checkout traffic only as an emergency mitigation; will start with a 10% canary for 15 minutes.
- We'll monitor session continuity and cookie behavior; if there are any cross-region session pins we'll fall back to token-based routing.

Marissa — please coordinate comms to Skyline PM and CS and keep them updated on timing for the canary.

I'll update within 10 minutes with the bridge link and recommended rollout plan.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-26T03:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: APAC checkout latency spike & 502s

On Thu, May 26, 2028 at 03:25, kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
> Thanks Liya — I'm on it.

Initial triage notes: apac-1 (cluster apac-1a) is showing KV cache pressure and a subset of nodes entering a degraded path causing 502s on long-running generation requests tied to the checkout pipeline. Networking looks healthy at the infra layer, but CPU/GPU scheduling anomalies align with a model-serving job that appears to be overutilizing the node pool.

Plan (short):
1) Kill offending long-running job group on apac-1 nodes and trigger node-level drain for 8 nodes showing >85% GPU/mem TLB churn.
2) Deploy route rule to redirect origin header for /v1/checkout/* from apac-1 -> eu-2 for 10% of traffic (canary) at 04:00 UTC.
3) Observe error-rate and tail latency for 15 minutes. If stable, increase to 40% and re-evaluate.

Risks/Notes: session affinity may cause user-visible retries for in-flight checkouts; recommend adding a short retry with idempotency key on the client side (we can patch edge config). Also attaching a route-table snapshot and a minimal canary rollout doc (canary-rollout-plan.md).

I'll stand up the bridge at 03:50 UTC and post the link.
—Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Liya Chen <liya@skylineretail.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-26T03:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: APAC checkout latency spike & 502s

Liya — I'm very sorry for the interruption. We have a short bridge open (https://drive.re/incident/skyline-apac-20280526) and our on-call infra team will execute a controlled geo-redirect canary for checkout traffic starting at 04:00 UTC.

What we will do now:
- 04:00 UTC: 10% canary to eu-2 for /v1/checkout/*
- 04:15 UTC: evaluate SLOs and customer-visible behavior
- 04:30 UTC: scale to 40% if stable or roll back immediately on regression

We will not change any tokens or credentials; this is only an edge routing change. Expect any in-flight sessions to get a single retry, but we will enable idempotency safeguards. I'll be your single point of contact for updates and will escalate to execs if this takes longer than 45 minutes.

—Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Liya Chen <liya@skylineretail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: skylineretail-ops@skylineretail.com
Date: 2028-05-26T04:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: APAC checkout latency spike & 502s

Thanks — the bridge link is in the ticket. We approve the 10% canary. Two asks:
1) Please confirm whether cookies set at the edge will be domain-bound (we use a CDN cookie that may not be valid for eu-2).
2) Rough ETA to full reset (40% or more) if canary looks good.

If you can get a 30–45 minute stabilization that will avoid a broader failover on our side.

Liya
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Liya Chen <liya@skylineretail.com>
Date: 2028-05-26T10:45:00Z
Subject: Exec summary & authorization: APAC geo-redirect

Summary for execs and Skyline leadership:
- Root impact: apac-1 node-level serving overload causing elevated tail latency and 502s for checkout pipeline impacting ~12% of APAC traffic.
- Action taken: controlled geo-redirect canary (apac->eu-2) executed at 04:00 UTC. 10% canary showed 60% reduction in tail latency and 502 rate dropped to background levels. 40% ramp completed at 04:22 UTC with continued improvement.
- Authorization: I'm authorizing a temporary sustained redirect to eu-2 for checkout for the next 6 hours while we drain and rebuild apac-1 nodes and run an extended post-mortem.

Next steps (owner):
- Aditya: complete drain and rebuild of 8 nodes (ETA 6 hours) and provide config diff for canary routing.
- Kimberly: draft customer-facing incident note and SLA credit recommendation (if applicable).
- Marissa: coordinate final comms to Skyline PM and ops and confirm session-cookie behavior with Skyline team.

I'll join the post-mortem and we will schedule a follow-up with Skyline for root-cause and prevention.

—Vivek Kulkarni
SVP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
